key: Agni bestows all vital power even as each man supplicates. He brings the Vasus strengthening gifts, and grants delight, in rest and stir, for every calling on the Gods.
s: Fourth in a hymn to Agni, the verse turns from his office as the worshipper’s messenger to his gifts; Sāyaṇa, on 8.39.4, reads the delight as happiness born of calm and of sense contact, and takes Agni as doing all, whatever god is invoked.

evidence.words: “ऊर्जाहुतिः अन्नेनाहूयमानोऽग्निः “वसूनां हविषां वासकानां यजमानानां “शं शान्तिनिमित्तं "योः विषययोगजनितं “च “मयः सुखं “दधे करोति । “विश्वस्यै “देवहूत्यै सर्वस्मै देवानां ह्वानाय च भवति । यः कश्चनापि देवो यदि हूयते अग्निरेव सर्वं करोतीत्यर्थः ।
evidence.gloss: Agni, invoked with food (ūrjāhutiḥ), makes (dadhe) for the Vasus, that is the sacrificers who hold the oblations, happiness (mayaḥ), both śam, caused by tranquillity, and yoḥ, born of contact with the objects of sense. He is there for every invocation of the gods: whatever god is invoked, Agni alone does everything; that is the meaning.

reason: The problem holds: the standing context clause describes the refrain and 8.39.2’s destroyers but never places the key verse, and ‘all the others’ has no referent. day.js shows 8.39.3 ends Agni’s praise as ‘the worshipper’s blissful messenger’ and 8.39.4 is the fourth verse, turning to what he bestows. Rewrote the plain sense to place the verse (‘Fourth in a hymn to Agni, the verse turns from his office as the worshipper’s messenger to his gifts’), dropping the unexplained refrain rather than carry ‘the others’ without a referent (the refuter’s wording also needed 46+ words with the reading intact). The Sāyaṇa half is unchanged. Re-opened packet.js veda 84 --verse 8.39.4 (revision 275528): śaṃ śāntinimittaṃ, yoḥ viṣayayogajanitaṃ ca mayaḥ sukham; yaḥ kaścanāpi devo yadi hūyate agnir eva sarvaṃ karoti; Wilson’s note names the gloss as Sāyaṇa’s. recheck (packet) FOUND; verse.js ok (8.39.4 at [658,4]); entry-check ok (44 words, no four-word run from the key).
